correctness.rationale: PASS: The product L_2(n)=∏_{q^e||n}q^(e-1)(q-2) shows for odd u>=5 that L_2(u)>=3, with equality exactly u=5,9,15. Hence D_2(u)>=4, with equality exactly those u. For p>=7, exponent a=1 gives D_2(p)-p=D_2(p-2)-2>=2, equality iff p-2∈{5,9,15}, or p=7,11,17. For a>=2 the first two iterates sum to at least p^a+(p-6)p^(a-2), and the third contributes >=3, so surplus >=4. Geometric sums handle p=2,3,5. Independent exact direct iterative checks covered 231 prime-power cases p<500, p^a<=200000 and found exactly those equality cases. Finite checks corroborate rather than prove the bounds.
